messages.subject: Permutation Testing query
parts:
Hey,

I had a quick question regarding permutations.

Background:
My cross consists of 2956 genetic markers across 16 chromosomes. I'm
interested only the in the interaction effect between a pair of
markers. From the paper referenced in the man-file for "scan-two",
permutation testing is conducted by keeping an individual's genotype
constant while permuting its phenotype value.

Question:
(1) Is this how permutation is conducted in the function scantwo?
(2) Am I correct in assuming that the third column returned by a
scantwo with perms is the correct threshold to use?
(3) The LOD threshold located in the third column is described as "for
each pair of chromosomes we take the difference between the maximum
full LOD and the maximum additive LOD, and then maximize this across
chromosome pairs"; by each "chromosome pair" does this mean each
marker pair?
(4) Is the LOD-score threshold returned simply the maximum
"interaction" LOD score across all marker pairs for that particular
phenotype?

Thank you very much,
Rohith Srivas

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Permutation Testing query
parts:
On Apr 28, 2008, at 5:15 PM, rsr...@gmail.com wrote:
> Background:
> My cross consists of 2956 genetic markers across 16 chromosomes. I'm
> interested only the in the interaction effect between a pair of
> markers. From the paper referenced in the man-file for "scan-two",
> permutation testing is conducted by keeping an individual's genotype
> constant while permuting its phenotype value.
>
> Question:
> (1) Is this how permutation is conducted in the function scantwo?

Yes, permutations with scantwo will permute phenotypes relative to
genotypes,
keeping the genotype data intact.

> (2) Am I correct in assuming that the third column returned by a
> scantwo with perms is the correct threshold to use?

The third column of the permutation results is for the epistasis LOD
score,
comparing the full two-locus model to the additive two-locus model.
I would go so far as to call it the "correct" threshold. Different
people
have different views on the appropriate treatment of two-dimensional,
two-QTL
genome scans.

> (3) The LOD threshold located in the third column is described as "for
> each pair of chromosomes we take the difference between the maximum
> full LOD and the maximum additive LOD, and then maximize this across
> chromosome pairs"; by each "chromosome pair" does this mean each
> marker pair?

No we mean chromosome pairs. We first maximize each of LOD[full] and
LOD[add've] across pairs of positions within a given pair of
chromosomes,
take the difference, and then maximize that difference across pairs of
chromosomes.

> (4) Is the LOD-score threshold returned simply the maximum
> "interaction" LOD score across all marker pairs for that particular
> phenotype?
